title: Roman Leptis Magna
summary: Leptis Magna, a Phoenician trading port from the 7th century BCE, grew under Rome into one of North Africa's finest cities, and the Severan emperors embellished it in the 3rd century CE. Its theatre was completed in 1 or 2 CE and its amphitheatre dedicated in 56 CE; drifting sand later buried much of it.

uncertainty.note: The pin is dated by the earliest dated Roman-era monument on the pages opened, the theatre (completed 1 or 2 CE, Livius). The span ends with the Severan embellishment in the 3rd century CE (UNESCO). ICOMOS says the Roman city was built under Augustus and Tiberius without years.

where.modern_name: Leptis Magna, Khoms, Murqub District, Libya

importance.justification: UNESCO World Heritage Site described as having the most complete and impressive Roman ruins in North Africa.

sources.title: Archaeological Site of Leptis Magna (World Heritage List no. 183)
sources.author: UNESCO World Heritage Centre

reviewer_note: No model written: no page I opened gave a height for the theatre, amphitheatre or any other single structure (Livius gives only the amphitheatre arena as 57 x 47 m; theatrum.de gave cavea 87.6 m but is a database I did not cite). The date span is a constructed pin from Livius and UNESCO, not a sourced founding date. Pin uses OSM's site point; UNESCO lists N32 38 17.988 E14 17 35.016 for the property.
